about: On-screen type that is part of the picture, with absolute frames (24 fps). Captions of spoken lines are not here: they come from lines.json. x and y are fractions of the frame; y is the baseline. Styles: prompt (serif, the opening sentence), doubt (serif italic), stamp (condensed capitals, four times caption size), stamp2 (twice), small (caption size), fine (source lines), quote (serif italic, typed when type is set: characters per frame), guess (grey italic prediction on a black card), tele and term (typewriter and terminal faces), hand (handwriting; color pencil makes it graphite), caption (a silent caption in the caption position), docked (THE FUTURE IS plus a completion, in the caption position), rect and sweep (the cyan block), steps (text that changes on given frames).

29 October 1969. Leonard Kleinrock's own account: 'the first message on the Internet was lo'. It went over the ARPANET, the network the internet grew from (see the True table). The day and month are left off the card so that it can be read in the time it has.

L and O arrived, and the far computer crashed on the G. White is what arrived; grey is what was still to come. About an hour later the whole word went through (Kleinrock; Duvall, BBC Future, 28 October 2024).

'They were able to do the full login about an hour later' (Kleinrock). The stamp lands on the beat, two frames before the chorus says We'll fix it. The hour is in the small line under it: the stamp alone has to be readable in ten frames.
a drawing of the signal, not data: 256 slits for the 256 electrodes in his speech motor cortex (NEJM, 14 August 2024). They are busiest while the sentence is being written from them.

events.note: the question to whoever is watching, one part on each of the last three clicks. Since v014 it is set in the film's serif italic, the face the film keeps for questions, larger than the sentence above it, so the last screen speaks in one voice (the user asked for better type here; until v013 it was heavy condensed capitals). On the last click the cursor comes to rest after the question mark and blinks there: it is the viewer's turn.
